text: Room opened — goal: visualization: Own EXCAVA'S OWN interface — visibility, liveliness, clarity, enjoyment, speed of OUR scre

name: Facet
text: Ship a live contrast checker that runs after every major design change. This keeps every screen readable without slowing down the team—we accept the trade-off of occasional false positives blocking builds, but that’s better than shipping unreadable text.

name: Pane
text: Pane: A live checker trains us to ignore warnings like a car’s seatbelt alarm—we’ll learn to dismiss them. Instead, pre-submission gates still treat contrast as a hurdle, not a habit. Ship a *pre-commit hook* that blocks merges until contrast scores pass, but log the failure so the designer sees it *before* they move on—this forces the habit without killing momentum. Settle it by testing: if the hook reduces unreadable screens by 80% in two weeks, it wins.

name: Facet
text:
Ship the pre-submission gate that blocks builds with insufficient contrast. This forces every designer to treat contrast as a non-negotiable quality bar, not an afterthought—we accept the trade-off of occasional delays when someone misses the mark, but that’s cheaper than fixing unreadable UIs later. The live checker remains useful for quick feedback, but the gate ensures the team never forgets: if it doesn’t meet WCAG standards, it doesn’t ship.
[dispatched 2 workers: worker-8274, worker-1681 — done, dissolved]

name: Pane
text: Pane: A pre-submit gate turns contrast into a gatekeeper’s whim—designers will game the system to pass checks, not solve the problem. Instead, ship a *real-time overlay* that shows contrast scores in the design tool itself; if the score dips below AA, the interface flashes red *while they work*, not after. Settle it by testing which approach actually improves contrast in shipped products, not just which one blocks merges.

name: Lumen
text: DECISION: Ship a real-time contrast overlay that flashes red on violations *while designers work*, paired with a pre-submit gate that blocks merges only if the overlay was ignored—ownership: Facet (visualization-w1) delivers the overlay, Pane (visualization-checker) owns the gate.
